items.title: Xcode 26.3 Integrates Claude Agent & OpenAI Codex — Agentic Coding Comes to Apple Dev
items.summary: Apple released Xcode 26.3 with native integration of Anthropic's Claude Agent and OpenAI's Codex directly in the IDE. The AI systems can autonomously write code, build projects, run tests, and iterate — turning Xcode into an agentic coding environment. This is Apple's biggest AI developer tooling move yet.
items.relevance: Huge for AVA development. Claude Agent inside Xcode means you could have AI autonomously building and testing SwiftUI views, running simulator tests, and iterating on the AVA app — all without leaving your IDE. Worth upgrading immediately.

items.title: Claude Code Fast Mode — 2.5x Faster Responses Now in Preview
items.summary: Anthropic rolled out a 'fast mode' for Claude Code powered by Opus 4.6, delivering up to 2.5x faster responses. Aimed at high-intensity tasks like debugging large codebases, reviewing files, and generating complex scripts. Currently in early research preview for users with additional usage enabled.
items.relevance: Speed has been the main friction point with Claude Code for quick iterations. 2.5x faster on debugging and code review could make the edit-test cycle on AVA much tighter. Worth enabling if you're on the preview list.

items.title: FreeStyle Libre 3 Sensor Recall — 7 Deaths, 860 Injuries from Incorrect Low Readings
items.summary: FDA expanded recall details on certain FreeStyle Libre 3 and Libre 3 Plus sensors that display glucose readings lower than actual levels. As of Jan 7, 2026, Abbott reported 860 serious injuries and 7 deaths associated with the faulty sensors. Specific model numbers are affected — readers and apps are not impacted.
items.relevance: Critical safety news for the T1D community. Falsely low CGM readings are dangerous — people skip treatment thinking they're fine. This reinforces why education tools like AVA matter: teaching people to recognize when something feels off vs what the device says.

items.title: Sequel Med Twiist Pump — Oreo-Sized, Tidepool Loop Algorithm, Apple Watch Control
items.summary: Deep dive on the Twiist insulin pump from Sequel Med. Uses sound waves (iiSure™ Technology) to measure each microdose of insulin, detects occlusions 9x faster than competitors. Size of an Oreo cookie (~2 oz). Powered by Tidepool Loop algorithm, compatible with Libre 3 Plus, controllable via iPhone app or Apple Watch. Approved for ages 6+.
items.relevance: Serious competitor to Omnipod. The Tidepool Loop algorithm is open-source-derived, Apple Watch control is slick, and the meal absorption profiles (fast/standard/slow with food emojis) are something AVA's simulation could model. Worth watching as a device to potentially support in AVA's Live Track.

items.title: Medtronic 780G Wins Expanded FDA Label — Now Covers Type 2, Ultra-Rapid Insulins, Abbott CGM
items.summary: Medtronic received expanded FDA clearance for its MiniMed 780G insulin pump, now covering Type 2 diabetes use, compatibility with Abbott's CGM platform, and support for ultra-rapid-acting insulins (Lyumjev, Fiasp, Merilog). This significantly broadens the 780G's addressable market.
items.relevance: Pumps expanding into Type 2 means the education market is growing fast. Every new pump user — T1 or T2 — needs to learn carb counting, insulin timing, and CGM interpretation. AVA's educational tools become relevant to a much larger audience.

items.title: OpenAI Codex Mac App — Native macOS Coding Agent That 'Builds Apps Over Days'
items.summary: OpenAI launched Codex as a native macOS app on Feb 3. Commands multiple AI coding agents simultaneously, runs shell commands in parallel, and supports personal skill loading from ~/.agents/skills. Positioned as a direct competitor to Claude Code with persistent multi-day project memory.
items.relevance: Worth trying alongside Claude Code. The skill-loading system (~/.agents/skills) is interesting — similar to Clawdbot's skill architecture. Multi-agent parallel execution could be useful for complex builds. Competition is making all these tools better.

items.title: India AI Impact Summit Next Week — Pichai, Gates, Jensen, Altman, 100+ Countries
items.summary: The largest global AI summit to date kicks off Feb 16-20 in New Delhi with 100+ countries, 15+ heads of state, and 100+ CEOs. Confirmed: Sundar Pichai, Bill Gates, Jensen Huang. Sam Altman attending closed-door sessions. India pushing 'impact-first' AI governance for the Global South.
items.relevance: Watch next week for major announcements. Every AI CEO in one room usually means product drops. Pichai may reveal Gemini updates, Jensen could announce Vera Rubin pricing, Altman's closed-door meetings hint at something big from OpenAI.

items.title: The Atlantic: AI Could 'Wipe Out Half of All Entry-Level White-Collar Jobs' in 1-5 Years
items.summary: Major Atlantic feature citing Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warning AI could drive unemployment up 10-20% and eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs within 1-5 years. UC Berkeley study shows AI is making people work MORE, not less — smaller teams absorbing more work as companies cut headcount under AI pretenses.
items.source: The Atlantic / UC Berkeley / Tech Brew
items.relevance: The labor disruption is real and accelerating. For an independent contractor like you, AI tools are a force multiplier — you're using them to build products, not being replaced by them. But worth considering: AVA could also serve as a training tool for healthcare workers being asked to do more with less.
